Subject: Inference Observability & Ops Tooling — POC test plan and next steps

Caleb — great to meet earlier. Quick recap from our discovery and a proposed POC scope so we can align on the tests that matter for Elara.

Top priorities you emphasized:
- Token-/request-level observability: per-route latency percentiles, per-token breakdown, and tail-latency diagnostics tied to request IDs.
- Cost visibility: per-route and per-customer cost attribution, and the ability to simulate billing for replayed traffic.
- Reliability and graceful degradation: failover to cheaper model variants, cross-region fallback, and controlled throttling.
- Compliance: retention windows for logs and KV cache behavior, SOC2 evidence points.

Competitive concerns you called out:
- Hyperscalers have scale but you lose token-level telemetry and fine-grained cost attributions; vendor lock-in on tooling is a concern.
- Some inference APIs show opaque batching behavior that makes latency cost tradeoffs hard to reason about.

Proposed POC (90–120 min technical session + 48–72 hr extended replay window):
1) End-to-end tracing: we’ll exercise requests through your app -> Redwood API -> model and show OpenTelemetry traces, per-token timings, and a trace-to-log correlation map. Goal: verify request-level debugability.
2) Replay & cost delta: replay 6 hours of a representative traffic slice and produce a per-route cost comparison (Redwood small-quantized model variant vs hyperscaler baseline). Goal: measurable cost delta and per-token accounting.
3) Failure/fallback test: simulate model OOM / node loss and validate Redwood’s automatic fallback to a compatible quantized variant and regional routing rules. Goal: no dropped requests, preserved SLOs.

Attachments: poc-test-matrix.xlsx (draft test matrix).

Next steps: Please confirm stakeholders who should be on the technical session (I’ve cc’d Aisha and Sergio from our side). We can run the session next week — we have open slots Tue/Wed 10–12 PT and Thu 1–3 PT.

Thanks,

Subject: Internal: technical test specs and competitive notes (Elara POC)

Internal notes — summarizing the tests I recommend we run and what to watch for. Pulling this into the poc test matrix (ops-test-spec.md attached).

1) Tracing & telemetry
- Redwood: full request-id flow, OpenTelemetry span per request and per model invocation, optional per-token timing exported as span attributes.
- Hyperscalers: typically provide request-level metrics and sampling-level traces but not deterministic per-token timings; harder to tie a single token event to app trace.
- Test metric: trace completeness ratio (spans with token_timing attribute / total spans) — target > 95%.

2) Replay & cost accounting
- Redwood: can enable per-route cost reporting, token counts, and apply quantization profiles to produce alternate cost projections.
- Hyperscalers often report compute time but not per-token billing breakdowns for composite prompts.
- Test metric: per-route unit-cost delta and variance over repeated replays.

3) Failure & fallback behavior
- Redwood: automatic model variant fallback (same API surface) and regional routing policy; KV cache persistence prevents cache cold-start for short failovers.
- Hyperscalers: failover often requires manual endpoint management or heavier infra changes.
- Test metric: percent of requests served within SLO during induced node failures.

4) Dashboards & alerting
- Redwood Console: token-level cost heatmaps, per-model latency percentiles, anomaly alerts tied to prompt-set regressions. Can push alerts to PagerDuty and webhook sinks.
- Hyperscalers: dashboards exist for infra metrics but stitching prompt-level quality regressions into alerts is more ad hoc.

Data access & infra notes:
- For the replay we will need the sanitized S3 slice and a short-lived role with read-only access. Mark will set this up.
- For SOC2 artifact request: prepare a scoped log retention export (dates + request ids only) — Amber will define the exact fields.

I attached ops-test-spec.md with actionable thresholds and the data hooks we need. I also recommend we prepare two comparison artifacts: (1) a short one-pager on telemetry coverage, (2) a CSV output of a small replay to show per-route billing.

— Sergio
